app.name: Salesforce (Sales Cloud / Salesforce Platform REST API)

appTypes.name: External Client App (ECA), local
appTypes.whenToUse: Prototype and your own org or a customer org you control. Created in Setup, External Client App Manager. This is now the only way to make a new app by default.

appTypes.name: External Client App, packaged (2nd generation package)
appTypes.whenToUse: Production for an agent product. You ship the ECA in a package so customer orgs can install it and admins can govern it.

appTypes.name: Connected App (legacy)
appTypes.whenToUse: Avoid. Creating new ones is off by default since Spring '26, and support ends in Summer '27 per secondary sources.

verdict.label: Self-serve, optional review
verdict.summary: You can create an External Client App yourself with no Salesforce approval, but each customer org's admin may have to install or approve it. The AppExchange security review applies only if you want a public listing.
verdict.nextStep: Sign up for a free Developer Edition org, then create an External Client App with scopes api and refresh_token and PKCE on.
verdict.customerSideGateNote: Salesforce admins control who can use an app through OAuth policies (admin-approved users, profiles, permission sets). Whether unpackaged, uninstalled apps from another org are blocked for customer users was not confirmed from official docs.

composio.note: Composio lists Salesforce under managed OAuth, so you can start today. Moving to your own app later only affects new connections. Existing users must reconnect.

stages.name: Prototype
stages.whoCanConnect: Users in the org that owns the app, plus any org where you or an admin set it up. A free Developer Edition org works.
stages.notes: Use https://login.salesforce.com for production orgs and https://test.salesforce.com for sandboxes.

stages.name: Production (any customer org)
stages.whoCanConnect: Users in customer orgs whose admins allow the app. Packaging the ECA is the expected route.
stages.notes: No Salesforce approval is needed to connect. AppExchange security review is needed only for a public listing; its timing was not confirmed. Partner apps used by more than two customer production orgs must meet extra OAuth controls.

scopeTiers.name: Standard data access
scopeTiers.effect: Lets your app call REST APIs as the user. No Salesforce review. The customer admin can still restrict who may authorize.

scopeTiers.name: Offline access
scopeTiers.effect: Issues refresh tokens for background work. For partner apps, rotation, a 30-day idle limit and an IP allowlist are mandatory.

scopeTiers.name: Specialty and Data Cloud APIs
scopeTiers.effect: Listed in the discovery document. Extra org features or licenses may be needed. Not confirmed to need review.

requirements.item: Salesforce org to host the app
requirements.detail: Free Developer Edition org from the signup page. Packaged distribution needs a long-lived org, not a scratch org.

requirements.item: HTTPS callback URL on your domain
requirements.detail: Register exact callback URLs on the app. Localhost is shown in official docs for dev tools. Wildcards are not documented here, so assume exact match.

requirements.item: PKCE, refresh token rotation, idle TTL, IP allowlist
requirements.detail: Required for partner apps used by more than two customer production orgs. A good baseline for any agent. You need static egress IPs for the allowlist.
Needed for AppExchange listing and security review. Exact checklist not confirmed.
Lets customer admins install and manage the app.

steps.title: Create a Developer Edition org
steps.detail: Open https://developer.salesforce.com/signup, register, and verify the email.

steps.title: Create an External Client App
steps.detail: In Setup, search External Client App Manager, click New External Client App, fill Basic Information, then tick Enable OAuth.

steps.title: Set callback URL and scopes
steps.detail: Enter your exact HTTPS callback URL. Select api, id, and refresh_token (offline_access). Tick Require PKCE.

steps.title: Copy consumer key and secret
steps.detail: Open the app, Settings tab, OAuth Settings, Consumer Key and Secret. Salesforce emails a verification code.

steps.title: Implement the auth code flow with PKCE
steps.detail: Send users to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize with code_challenge (S256). Exchange at /services/oauth2/token. Store the instance_url returned per user.

steps.title: Handle refresh token rotation
steps.detail: Enable rotation and the 30-day idle limit. Save each new refresh token, serialize refresh calls per user, refresh before day 30.

steps.title: Set the refresh token IP allowlist
steps.detail: Add your server egress ranges (256 IPs max in total). Do not use it with localhost or custom URL scheme callbacks.

steps.title: Package the ECA
steps.detail: Create a second-generation package containing the ECA in a long-lived org. Share the install link with customer admins.

steps.title: Ask customer admins to install and set policies
steps.detail: Admin installs the package and sets OAuth Policies: permitted users, profiles, permission sets.

steps.title: Optional: AppExchange security review
steps.detail: Only for a public listing. Follow the ISVforce guide submission guidance.

blockers.symptom: New Connected App button is missing or greyed out
blockers.cause: Spring '26 turned off new Connected App creation by default.
blockers.fix: Create an External Client App instead.
blockers.escalation: Salesforce Support can re-enable it for now, but this is temporary.

blockers.cause: Wrong consumer key, or the app is not available in that org.
blockers.fix: Check the key, and use test.salesforce.com for sandboxes. Confirm the app is installed in the customer org.

blockers.cause: Rotation made the old token single-use, parallel refresh calls raced, 30-day idle limit passed, or the IP is not allowlisted.
blockers.fix: Serialize refreshes, store the newest token, refresh before day 30, check allowlist.

blockers.symptom: Customer user cannot authorize the app
blockers.cause: Admin policy limits permitted users or the app is not installed.
blockers.fix: Ask the admin to install the package and pre-authorize profiles or permission sets.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails after enabling PKCE
blockers.fix: Add S256 challenge on authorize and the verifier on token request.

drafts.title: Admin install note for customers
drafts.body: Our assistant connects to your Salesforce org through an External Client App. Please install the package from the link, then in Setup, External Client App Manager, open the app, Policies, and set Permitted Users to admin-approved. Add the profiles or permission sets that may use it. Scopes: api (read and write records as the user), refresh_token (stay connected without re-login), id (identify the user). We never see passwords. You can revoke access at any time by removing the profile or deleting the user's OAuth token.

drafts.title: Scope justification
drafts.body: api: needed to read and update CRM records the user asks our assistant to handle. refresh_token: needed so scheduled tasks work when the user is offline. id: identifies the connected user and org. We request no other scopes. Tokens are encrypted at rest, refresh tokens are rotated on each use, and refresh calls come only from our allowlisted IPs.

uncertainties.howToResolve: Test with a second Developer org, and read Salesforce Help on ECA distribution and uninstalled app approval.

evidence.claim: Partner ECAs/Connected Apps used by more than two customer production orgs must enable PKCE, refresh token rotation, 30-day idle refresh TTL and refresh token IP allowlist, due May 11, 2026; new Connected Apps cannot be created from Spring '26.
evidence.sourceTitle: Secure Your Connected Apps and External Client Apps (ISVforce Guide)

evidence.claim: ECAs are created in Setup via External Client App Manager, with OAuth scopes (api, web, refresh_token/offline_access), callback URL, and admin OAuth policies for permitted users, profiles and permission sets; consumer key needs email verification.
evidence.sourceTitle: Create an External Client App in Your Org (Salesforce DX Developer Guide)
